overview.title: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose And INA
overview.definition: The Indian National Army (INA) or Azad Hind Fauj was an armed force formed by Indian nationalists in 1942 in Southeast Asia, with the objective of securing Indian independence from British rule through military action, led by Subhash Chandra Bose.
overview.importanceInUpsc: This topic is a perennial favorite in UPSC Prelims (chronology, leadership, locations) and Mains (impact on British withdrawal, communal harmony, and the role of radical nationalism).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose And INA.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **First INA Phase**: Initiated by **Mohan Singh** and **Fujiwara** (Japanese Major) in 1942 after the fall of Singapore. 
• **Second INA Phase**: Subhash Chandra Bose arrived in Singapore (July 1943) and took over leadership from **Rash Behari Bose**. 
• **Provisional Government**: Established in Singapore (Oct 1943) as the **Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind**, recognized by Axis powers. 
• **Key Metric**: The INA comprised roughly 40,000-50,000 soldiers, including the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment** (all-women combat unit).

items.definition: Formed by Bose in 1939 after resigning from Congress presidency; served as the radical faction within the nationalist movement.
Broadcasts from Germany and later Singapore to boost morale and communicate with the Indian public.
Congress formed the INA Defense Committee (Bhulabhai Desai, Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru) to defend the accused, turning the trial into a political platform.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Military Campaign**: The Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944) aimed to enter India via Burma. 
• **Socio-Political Integration**: INA promoted secularism; soldiers were drawn from all religions and regions, creating a unified national identity.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of air support, supply line failures, and the defeat of Japan in WWII. 
• **Legacy**: The INA trials proved that the British could no longer rely on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-R-M' (Singapore, Rash Behari, Mohan Singh). 
• **Decoded Meaning**: Mohan Singh started it, Rash Behari organized it, Subhash led it.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'INA Defense Committee' with the 'INA leadership'. Remember, the Committee was formed by the Congress, not by Bose.
Mains Value Addition: Use the quote 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom' to highlight the psychological impact of Bose's rhetoric on the Indian masses.

keyTakeaways: The INA was a military force that transformed into a political symbol of anti-colonial resistance.
The INA trials were the 'last nail in the coffin' of British rule in India.
Bose's leadership emphasized secularism and gender equality (Rani of Jhansi Regiment).
